clue.text: Has dispute about right usage

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone quarrels over the correct way to use a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges R plus USAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to have a dispute, a verb phrase meaning to quarrel.

clue.text: Maybe this is meant as incentive not to procrastinate

definitions.text: Maybe this is meant as incentive not to procrastinate

parts.words: Maybe this is meant as incentive not to procrastinate
parts.note: the clue describes a proverb urging prompt action; 'meant' hints at mending clothes, sewing a small tear before it grows

explanation.surface: Musing on what spurs a person to stop putting things off.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a small repair done promptly saves a larger one later; 'meant' doubles as a near-sound of 'mend', fitting the sewing image.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is a classic admonition against delay, urging timely action to prevent bigger problems.

clue.text: Overindulge in food or in egg flip

indicators.note: in places the small word inside the turned-over egg
flip means the word egg is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice not to overdo it with food, including an egg flip drink.
explanation.walkthrough: An egg flip is also a drink of beaten egg, which disguises 'flip' as the reversal signal; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself greedily with food.

clue.text: A decent performance carried out

indicators.note: a performance puts the words through their paces, signalling a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Praise for a respectable stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' rearranges A DECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enacted has been put into effect or performed, i.e. carried out.

clue.text: Dog Star

definitions.meaning: a dog, here the collie heroine of the films
a star, a celebrated performer on screen

explanation.surface: A two-word caption naming the brightest star, Sirius.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Sirius, the Dog Star; instead the clue is two separate definitions of the famous collie of film and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie was a collie, so a dog, and also a screen celebrity who headlined many films.

clue.text: Feeler from worker girl rejected

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect, a stock crossword equivalence

indicators.note: rejected means the girl's name is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone sends out a feeler, only to be turned down by a working girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal; 'from' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an insect's sensory feeler on the head.

clue.text: Fan fire?

definitions.meaning: to fan is to rouse or intensify, as in fanning the flames
to fire is to inspire or excite, as in firing the imagination

explanation.surface: Is a fan blowing on a fire meant to make it burn?
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns, but each is a verb: to fan interest and to fire enthusiasm both mean to rouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate is to arouse or excite, as fanning or firing up does.

clue.text: Point learnt afresh for all time

parts.note: E, East, is a compass point

indicators.note: afresh means the letters are set out anew, rearranged

explanation.surface: A lesson learnt again is learnt for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afresh' is the anagram signal, and 'Point' means a compass point, here East.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means everlasting, lasting for ever.

clue.text: It comes to something when Dad's upset and out of bed

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: up means out of bed, risen

explanation.surface: Things are serious when an upset father has got out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DADS into ADDS; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: When a sum adds up it totals something, and an idea that adds up makes sense.

clue.text: Standard wear for officers and NCOs

definitions.text: Standard wear for officers and NCOs

parts.words: Standard wear for officers and NCOs
parts.note: a standard is a flag; officers wear stars as rank badges and NCOs wear stripes, so the flag is described by the insignia

explanation.surface: A description of the ordinary uniform worn by army ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as 'regular', but it means a flag: the US flag, whose name joins the badges of commissioned officers and non-commissioned officers (NCOs).
explanation.definitionFit: The American national flag is named after its starred canton and striped field, matching rank insignia.

clue.text: Second-class in an exam — that's the most hopeful view

indicators.note: in places the second-class grade inside the words for an exam

parts.note: an exam is a test, so A TEST
B is a second-class grade or mark

explanation.surface: A student reflects that a second-class result is the best they can hope for.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking the most optimistic outlook possible, as in 'at best, a draw'.

clue.text: Turn buns when cooked and well browned

indicators.note: cooking reworks ingredients, signalling that the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Baking instructions: flip the buns once they are nicely browned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' rearranges TURN BUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that is sunburnt is reddened or tanned by the sun, a jocular sense of thoroughly browned.

clue.text: Animal disinfectant mixed deep inside a vessel

indicators.note: inside places the jumbled letters within the word for a vessel

parts.note: a ship is a vessel

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe for a farmyard disinfectant blended in a deep container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' is the anagram signal and 'inside' the container signal; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep dip is the chemical wash farmers use to rid flocks of parasites.

clue.text: Cheerful midshipman goes on leave

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is a Captain Marryat sea novel, so the midshipman is Easy
going is departing, as one does on leave

explanation.surface: A naval cadet, happy at heart, sets off on shore leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Midshipman Easy' is an 1836 naval novel by Frederick Marryat, the source of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: An easygoing person is relaxed and good-humoured, so loosely cheerful.

clue.text: A Saudi, say, takes the French to be cultivated

parts.note: a Saudi is an example of an Arab
LE is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A man from Saudi Arabia adopts French ways to become refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' suggests refinement, but here it means farmed land.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is suitable for ploughing and growing crops, i.e. fit for cultivation.

clue.text: Wager about a dumb animal being a dog

indicators.note: about means the bet goes round the animal, enclosing it

parts.note: a wager is a bet
an ass, the donkey, is proverbially a dumb animal

explanation.surface: A bet placed on a stupid creature that turns out to be a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'being a' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hound breed with long ears.

clue.text: Anti-cooking, anti-gas

indicators.note: cooking signals the letters are mixed up like ingredients, rearranged

explanation.surface: A slogan opposing gas cookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges ANTIGAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means being opposed to it, the sense of anti as a preposition.

clue.text: Fish in river with spear

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
the id is a variant name of the ide, a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone spears a fish in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a river in the English Midlands; ID, also spelt IDE, is a freshwater fish listed in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, like Neptune's.

clue.text: Extra fashionable line in trousers

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a crease is the pressed line down trouser legs

explanation.surface: A dandy's extra-sharp trouser crease is the latest fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is an addition or extra amount, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Latins put out or put in office

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Latin speakers are expelled or else given power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges LATINS. INSTAL is the British spelling of install.
explanation.definitionFit: To instal someone is to place them formally in a post or office.

clue.text: Trick examination question

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: An exam paper containing a deliberately misleading question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'question' looks like a noun, but it is a verb: to dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a claim is to challenge or dispute it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Odd way to travel about

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
to range is to roam or wander about

explanation.surface: Wandering around is an unusual way to get anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means unusual or peculiar, a synonym of odd.

clue.text: Cheap items don't allow profits

parts.note: to bar is to prohibit, not allow
gains are profits

explanation.surface: A shop selling goods so cheaply it makes no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargains are goods bought cheaply, at a good price.

clue.text: Drains designed to reach the lowest depths

indicators.note: designed suggests something arranged to a new plan, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sewer system built to reach right down to the deepest levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges DRAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nadir is the lowest point, so plural nadirs are the lowest depths.

clue.text: Noise and energy seen in dog that's wild

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A racket and liveliness are noticed in an untamed dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is a link here, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is Australia's wild dog.

clue.text: See 1 down
Things loose women won't wear?

parts.note: playful reading: a loose garment is the opposite of a close-fitting one, so women in loose clothes skip the snug leg-wear; 'loose women' suggests something racier

explanation.surface: A remark about what promiscuous women refuse to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose women' suggests immoral ones; read literally it is just women dressed loosely, who would not wear something close-fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are close-fitting leg garments, the opposite of anything loose.

clue.text: Out of the office, but ready to receive calls

definitions.meaning: away from work, in one's own house

explanation.surface: An employee is away from work but still available by phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calls' suggests phone calls, but the second sense is social calls: visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at home is not at work, and a host who is at home receives visitors.
